papers.title: Predicting Rates of Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with Brain- and Cardiac-Imputed Transcripts.
papers.abstract: Severe cognitive decline due to dementia is an important clinical indicator signaling neurodegeneration. Predicting cognitive decline rates can be useful in establishing prognosis and modifying treatment regimens. The rate of decline is highly variable across patients with dementia and may be determined by an interplay of many factors. This variability poses challenges to existing tools for predicting disease progression. Changes in heart and brain tissue have been associated with cognitive decline, yet tissue-specific molecular data are difficult to obtain. In this study, we sought to estimat
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint develops a method to predict the rate of cognitive decline in older adults by imputing brain- and cardiac-tissue-specific gene expression from more accessible data, since directly sampling these tissues is impractical. The approach leverages the known associations between heart and brain tissue changes and cognitive decline to build predictive models of disease progression. The work aims to improve prognosis and treatment planning for dementia patients, whose decline rates vary widely.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Natural BACE1 Inhibitors with Enzymatic and Cellular Validation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by excessive accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides in the brain. Beta-secretase 1 (BACE1), the rate-limiting enzyme in the amyloidogenic processing pathway of amyloid precursor protein (APP), has been widely recognized as an important therapeutic target for reducing Aβ production. In the present study, nine machine learning-based predictive models for BACE1 inhibitors were constructed using Naïve Bayes (NB) and Recursive Partitioning (RP) algorithms. Subsequently, internal and external validations were conducte
papers.summary: This study built nine machine learning models (Naïve Bayes and Recursive Partitioning) to predict BACE1 inhibitors, a key Alzheimer's drug target, and used them to discover natural compounds that were then validated enzymatically and in cells. The work demonstrates a practical ML-guided pipeline for identifying natural-product BACE1 inhibitors with experimental confirmation.

papers.title: MacroTox: A Macroscopic Graph Topology-Based Multimodal Learning Framework for Robust Molecular Toxicity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Despite breakthroughs in predicting acute organ toxicities, advanced computational models continue to struggle with complex, insidious end points like drug-induced bone toxicity. A fundamental limitation of most supervised pipelines is their failure to explicitly model intermolecular similarities during task-specific training. Neglecting this macroscopic topology of the chemical space leads to fragmented latent representations, poor generalization, and high false negative rates. To address this, we propose MacroTox, a macroscopic topology-driven multimodal deep learning framework. Beyond intra
papers.summary: MacroTox is a multimodal deep learning framework that explicitly models intermolecular similarities (macroscopic topology of chemical space) to improve molecular toxicity prediction, especially for complex endpoints like drug-induced bone toxicity. By incorporating this global chemical-space structure during training, it aims to produce more coherent latent representations and reduce false negatives compared to standard supervised pipelines.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representation-based models, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information critical for accurate CPI prediction. This could improve early-stage drug discovery by enabling more reliable large-scale interaction screening.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study examines how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This study synthesized two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and cyclic chalcone derivatives using an environmentally friendly choline hydroxide catalyst, then tested them against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. Compound 11e showed the strongest inhibition (IC50 = 0.599 µg/mL), and molecular docking was used to explore how these compounds bind to the enzyme.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of nine diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer testing. The compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against breast cancer cells in vitro, with additional in vivo and in silico analyses. The work aims to identify structurally diverse anticancer agents for breast cancer treatment.

papers.title: Rational High-Throughput Screening of Cocrystals: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework Based on Morgan Fingerprints and Cross-Attention.
papers.abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high blindness in traditional screening methods, insufficient granularity of feature representation, and poor interpretability of existing machine learning prediction models in the field of cocrystal research and development, we propose a cocrystal prediction method based on Morgan fingerprints and the cross-attention mechanism. First, a high-quality cocrystal data set is constructed, and Morgan fingerprints are employed to characterize molecular structures. Subsequently, a fingerprint-driven cross-attention model is developed to capture the feature interactio
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that predicts cocrystal formation by combining Morgan fingerprints with a cross-attention mechanism. The model aims to reduce the trial-and-error nature of traditional cocrystal screening and improve interpretability of predictions. A curated high-quality cocrystal dataset was constructed to train and evaluate the approach.

papers.title: Discovery of Selective Small-Molecule Ligands of SV2C by AI-Enhanced Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (SV2C) is enriched in dopaminergic neurons and implicated in Parkinson's disease, but no selective small-molecule probes exist for it. Lacking a full-length SV2C structure, we built a homology model from SV2A cryo-EM templates and used molecular dynamics to characterize its conformational landscape. An AI-enhanced virtual screening pipeline, validated on a curated SV2A benchmark, was applied to 5.96 million commercial compounds, prioritizing 94 candidates for experimental testing. Of 71 compounds tested in an orthogonal biophysical assay cascade, 22 were active
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a homology model of the synaptic vesicle protein SV2C, which is linked to Parkinson's disease but lacks selective chemical probes, and used molecular dynamics plus an AI-enhanced virtual screening pipeline to screen 5.96 million compounds. They prioritized 94 candidates, tested 71 in biophysical assays, and identified 22 active compounds, providing a starting point for selective SV2C ligands.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Candidate Drug Targets in Endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder affecting 5-10% of women of reproductive age and is associated with chronic pain and infertility. While research has mainly focused on local lesions, systemic immune dysfunction is increasingly implicated in disease pathogenesis. This study employs single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from women with endometriosis and unaffected controls, combined with integrative analysis of publicly available datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissues, to uncover immune dysregulation and therapeutic targ
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from women with endometriosis and controls, combined with public datasets from menstrual blood and endometrial tissue, to characterize systemic immune dysregulation. The analysis identifies altered immune cell populations and candidate drug targets, suggesting that endometriosis involves broader immune dysfunction beyond local lesions.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer and antibacterial activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. The work identifies these scaffolds as potential leads for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover new small-molecule ligands that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3,353 compounds and prioritized candidate hits, then validated their stability through MD simulations. The work offers a computational pipeline for identifying inhibitors that may work against ligand-independent ERα activation.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Identifying Natural Product-Derived Cathepsin K Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent skeletal disorder characterized by excessive bone resorption and an increased risk of fragility fracture. Cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts, is an established target for anti-resorptive drug development. Here, an integrated computational workflow comprising virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, and drug-likeness/ADMET prediction was used to prioritize natural product-derived CatK ligands from th
papers.summary: This study uses computational drug discovery methods—virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA binding energy calculations, and ADMET prediction—to identify natural product-derived compounds that inhibit cathepsin K, a protease target for treating osteoporosis. The workflow prioritizes candidate ligands from a natural product library as potential anti-resorptive therapeutics, though experimental validation is not reported.

papers.title: Donor-Type-Dependent Heterogeneity of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Lung Transplantation: A Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Interaction Analysis of DCD Versus DBD Lungs.
papers.abstract: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donor lungs are widely used in lung transplantation yet managed as equivalent with respect to ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), despite fundamentally different ischemic backgrounds: warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD donors.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-cohort transcriptomic interaction analysis to show that ischemia-reperfusion injury in lung transplantation differs fundamentally between donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) lungs. The findings suggest DCD and DBD lungs should not be managed as equivalent, since their injury responses are driven by distinct biological mechanisms.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard MLP in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It is evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and other representative methods. The work tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves molecular representation for DTA tasks.

papers.title: Multi-Endpoint Prediction of Bioactivity and ADMET Properties Coupled with Multi-Objective Optimization in Molecular Descriptor Space for Candidate ERα Antagonists.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Candidate estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) antagonists should combine strong inhibitory activity with favorable absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET)-related properties. This study developed an integrated framework for multi-endpoint prediction, multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space, and prioritization of feasible solutions. Methods: A dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 molecular descriptors, pIC50 values, and five binary ADMET-related endpoints was analyzed. Key descriptors were identified through two-stage cross-method and cross-e
papers.summary: This study builds an integrated computational framework that predicts multiple bioactivity and ADMET endpoints for potential ERα antagonists and then uses multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space to prioritize candidate compounds. Using a dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 descriptors, the authors identify key molecular features that balance strong ERα inhibition with favorable drug-like properties. The approach aims to streamline early-stage drug discovery by simultaneously optimizing efficacy and safety-related endpoints.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: SF-DTI is a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic representations, and uses progressive cross-modal refinement to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities. The approach aims to better exploit complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders, improving DTI prediction accuracy for drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Brightfield Detection of Anti-Fibrotic Effects in a 3D Retinal Fibrosis Model.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid and microtissue models are increasingly used in phenotypic drug discovery, yet their scalability for high-throughput screening often remains limited, constrained by the cost and complexity of conventional imaging-based readouts. Here, we present a morphology-based screening approach using low-resolution brightfield images of human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues (hRPE-MTs) to identify fibrotic and non-fibrotic phenotypes. The results of this study demonstrate that extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids enables quan
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning approach that uses low-resolution brightfield images of 3D human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues to distinguish fibrotic from non-fibrotic phenotypes. By extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids, the method enables scalable, cost-effective screening for anti-fibrotic compounds without expensive imaging readouts.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the antifungal protein NFAP2 from Aspergillus fischeri as a guide to identify fungus-specific protein targets in Candida albicans, including glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase. The authors then apply structure-based drug repurposing to find existing compounds that could inhibit these targets, offering a faster route to new antifungal therapies against drug-resistant Candida infections.

papers.title: Using structure to evaluate the accuracy and transferability of machine learning potentials of biomolecules.
papers.abstract: Molecular simulation is a powerful tool to describe chemical and physical processes across length scales. Fundamental tradeoffs between the accuracy of quantum mechanics and speed of classical models makes simulating biosystems very difficult. Machine learning potentials (MLPs) offer a potential solution which combines the accuracy of electronic structure theory with the computational scaling of classical approaches. Applying MLPs to biosystems could unlock new developments in drug discovery, biological mechanisms and interactions. Despite this promise, rigorous benchmarks are needed to determ
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks machine learning potentials (MLPs) for biomolecular simulation, using structural criteria to assess both accuracy and transferability across different molecular systems. It highlights the need for rigorous validation before MLPs can reliably replace quantum or classical methods in biological applications. The work provides guidance on where MLPs succeed and where they fail when applied to biosystems.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily model
papers.summary: This review traces how AI has been applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics across three generations: classical chemometrics/machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with LLMs only at the periphery. It highlights a paradox: despite being the omics layers closest to drug action, metabolomics and lipidomics have been slow to adopt modern AI, largely due to the lack of a closed molecular reference and standardized datasets.

papers.title: ProDTI: Prior-Guided Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Robust Drug-Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate Drug-Target Interaction (DTI) prediction is critical for drug discovery. While deep learning advances this field, the fundamental lack of verified negative interactions inevitably causes biased risk estimation. Although formulating DTI prediction as a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning problem is theoretically sound, directly applying PU learning to deep models suffers from early-stage optimization instability and decision boundary ambiguity.
papers.summary: ProDTI addresses the problem of drug-target interaction prediction when only positive interactions are verified and negatives are unknown, by framing it as a positive-unlabeled learning task with prior guidance. The method aims to overcome the optimization instability and ambiguous decision boundaries that arise when PU learning is naively applied to deep models. This offers a more robust approach to DTI prediction for drug discovery.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking (GNPS) to characterize the metabolite profile of Scoparia dulcis aerial parts and identify bioactive constituents with anti-inflammatory potential. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were combined with experimental validation to elucidate the anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The integrated approach revealed specific compounds and pathways underlying the herb's traditional use for inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Using molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and in vitro assays, the authors assess its ability to inhibit NorA and MepA efflux pumps that reduce antibiotic efficacy. The work identifies a promising natural-product-derived scaffold for combating antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized seventeen thymol-based derivatives by esterifying thymol with various cinnamoyl molecules, then tested their anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines and normal fibroblasts. The most promising compound, TM7, showed notable anti-proliferative effects, and molecular docking studies were used to explore its potential binding interactions with cancer targets.

papers.title: Discovery and biological characterization of 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype targeting yellow fever virus and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that inhibits yellow fever virus (YFV) by targeting the host protein casein kinase 2 (CK2) rather than the virus itself. The compound was synthesized, chemically validated, and shown to have antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in cell culture, suggesting host-directed antiviral potential.

papers.title: Selective PTP1B inhibition by A-1331852: Uncompetitive kinetics and computational evidence for C-terminal engagement.
papers.abstract: Selective inhibition of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a well-established target in metabolic and oncological signaling pathways, is limited by its 74% active-site identity with the closely related phosphatase TCPTP. Repurposing the clinical-stage Bcl-xL BH3 mimetic A-1331852, we identify it as a potent PTP1B inhibitor demonstrating a selectivity margin of at least 50-fold over TCPTP (IC₅₀ = 4.0 μM vs >200 μM). Kinetic analysis reveals uncompetitive inhibition consistent with recognition of a substrate-induced binding site. Docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MD) of fu
papers.summary: The clinical-stage Bcl-xL inhibitor A-1331852 was found to also inhibit the phosphatase PTP1B with at least 50-fold selectivity over the closely related TCPTP, a major challenge for PTP1B drug development. Kinetic analysis indicates uncompetitive inhibition, suggesting it binds a substrate-induced site rather than the active site, and docking plus 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations support engagement of the C-terminal region.

papers.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidin
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports a hybrid strategy that combines deep-learning-driven de novo protein design with directed evolution to create engineered haemoproteins capable of new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination, yielding chiral piperidine products. The work demonstrates that design and evolution can be used synergistically rather than separately to access enzyme chemistry not found in nature.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: This paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It specifically addresses class imbalance, a common problem in this prediction task, and aims to improve on existing methods. The tool is positioned as a cheaper, faster alternative to experimental screening for drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Novel Flavonoid Senotherapeutics Identified by Phenotypic Drug Discovery Reduce Senescence and Improve Multiple Markers of Healthspan.
papers.abstract: Senescent cells are a key driver of aging and contribute to many age-related diseases. Senolytics, agents that selectively eliminate senescent cells, offer a promising therapeutic strategy to treat age-related diseases but face significant barriers to clinical translation. Fisetin, a natural flavonoid senolytic, has progressed to clinical trials but is limited by suboptimal efficacy and poor bioavailability. To address these challenges, we developed two novel fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, using an integrative phenotypic drug discovery approach. These compounds exhi
papers.summary: Researchers used phenotypic drug discovery to create two new fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, designed to overcome fisetin's poor efficacy and bioavailability. These compounds reduce senescence and improve multiple healthspan markers, offering a potentially more translatable senolytic strategy for age-related diseases.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is an underexplored anticancer target, and the work demonstrates a hybrid computational pipeline for discovering novel inhibitors from marine sources.

papers.title: A multiparametric in vitro strategy for small molecule drug-induced liver injury risk mitigation in early drug development.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major cause of preclinical and clinical attrition, reflecting persistent gaps in the predictive translation of preclinical safety data to human outcomes. To address these gaps, we established a refined multiparametric framework for early DILI risk prediction using a balanced reference set of 170 drugs with established clinical outcomes. Thirty physicochemical, mechanistic endpoints, and exposure-related features were systematically evaluated to identify high-specificity predictors of intrinsic DILI risk. Cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes and h
papers.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
papers.summary: This study develops a multiparametric in vitro framework to predict drug-induced liver injury (DILI) risk early in drug development, using a balanced set of 170 drugs with known clinical outcomes. By evaluating 30 physicochemical, mechanistic, and exposure-related features, the authors identify high-specificity predictors of intrinsic DILI risk, including cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes. The approach aims to reduce late-stage attrition by improving the translation of preclinical safety data to human outcomes.

papers.title: Beyond affinity: AI-supported developability assessment and multi-objective optimization in antibody development.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies are a major class of medicines, but high target affinity alone does not ensure manufacturability, stability, safety, or clinical success. Developability has therefore become a central constraint in antibody engineering and has pushed the field beyond affinity-first screening toward multi-objective decision-making. Machine-learning-based models increasingly integrate antibody sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to estimate properties such as affinity, specificity, aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before exper
papers.summary: This review argues that therapeutic antibody development must move beyond simple affinity optimization to multi-objective developability assessment. It surveys how machine-learning models integrate sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to predict properties like aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before experimental testing.

papers.title: GCF-anchored and target-oriented mining of metagenomic BGC space for bioactive product discovery.
papers.abstract: Microbial natural products are vital for drug discovery, yet pervasive genomic fragmentation and data volume hinder the translation of metagenomic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into therapeutic leads. We present metasynBGC, a target-oriented framework that employs a "function-first" logic using experimentally validated gene cluster families (GCFs) as evolutionary templates and functional beacons. This dual-path strategy enables (i) template-guided reconstruction of fragmented BGCs via conserved biosynthetic synteny, and (ii) high-resolution prioritization of complete BGCs based on therapeu
papers.summary: The authors present metasynBGC, a target-oriented framework that uses experimentally validated gene cluster families (GCFs) as templates and functional beacons to mine metagenomic biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) space. The dual-path strategy reconstructs fragmented BGCs via conserved biosynthetic synteny and prioritizes complete BGCs for therapeutic potential, aiming to accelerate the translation of metagenomic natural products into drug leads.

papers.title: Brewing Anxiety: Caffeine-Induced Thigmotaxis in Zebrafish Larvae.
papers.abstract: Thigmotaxis, or edge preference, is widely used as a measure of anxiety in vertebrate model systems. However, variability in this behavior limits its utility as a scalable measure for anxiolytic drug discovery. In the current study, we examine caffeine-induced thigmotaxis, using 5-day-old zebrafish larvae as a model system.
papers.summary: This study examines whether caffeine, a known anxiogenic compound, induces thigmotaxis (edge-preference behavior) in 5-day-old zebrafish larvae, a behavior commonly used as an anxiety readout in vertebrate models. The authors aim to characterize variability in this response, which currently limits its usefulness for scalable anxiolytic drug discovery.

papers.title: Targeting a Leukemia-Relevant Protein-Protein Interface: N-Aryl Anthranilic Acids as Disruptors of the c-Myb-CBP/p300 KIX Interaction.
papers.abstract: The interaction between c-Myb and the CBP/p300 KIX domain is a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represents an attractive target for small-molecule intervention. In this study, we applied an integrated computational-experimental strategy to identify new N-aryl anthranilic acid disruptors of the c-Myb-KIX protein-protein interaction. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX (PDB 2AGH), and the top hits were further evaluated by MD simulations, MM/PBSA, FEL, and ADMET analyses. This
papers.summary: This study uses computational screening (docking, MD simulations, MM/PBSA, and ADMET analysis) of a 3,656-compound N-aryl anthranilic acid library to identify small molecules that disrupt the c-Myb–CBP/p300 KIX protein-protein interaction, a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia. The work nominates new chemical scaffolds as potential disruptors of this leukemia-relevant interface, though experimental validation of the top hits appears limited.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the anti-inflammatory potential of Cotula cinerea essential oil using GC-MS profiling, in vivo rat experiments, histology, and computational docking. The oil, rich in trans-thujone, reduced liver and kidney inflammation indices and improved red blood cell and hemoglobin levels in BTU-treated rats. Computational analysis supported the observed anti-inflammatory effects by identifying likely molecular targets.

papers.title: Synthesis and Cytotoxic Activity of 1,3-Selenazole-2-Amine Derivatives With Computational ADMET Profiling.
papers.abstract: A set of newly developed 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives (1-4) was prepared via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization of appropriately substituted α-bromoacetophenones with selenourea under reflux conditions. The synthesized compounds were tested for cytotoxic activity in HT-29 (colon cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), and L929 (mouse fibroblast) cell lines using the MTT assay. The compounds induced weak to moderate cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells. Among them, compound 4 showed cytotoxic activity with IC50 value of 171.10 µM, while no appreciable activity was observed against HT-29 cells (IC50 > 30
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of four new 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization and evaluates their cytotoxicity against colon cancer (HT-29), breast cancer (MCF-7), and normal fibroblast (L929) cell lines. The compounds showed only weak to moderate activity, with the best compound (4) having an IC50 of 171.10 µM against MCF-7 and no appreciable activity against HT-29. Computational ADMET profiling was also performed to predict drug-likeness properties.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo (rodent behavioral tests), and in silico (molecular docking) approaches, with relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant capacity and behavioral effects consistent with potential neuropharmacological activity, though it was far less potent than the ascorbic acid control.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches offer new opportunities, much of the evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Enzymatic N-deacylation is the predicted membrane-disruption switch for sphingomyelin: a falsifiable in-silico framework for sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS.
papers.abstract: Sphingolipid dysregulation is an emerging feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but no systematic method separates species that may worsen axon-myelin membrane integrity from matter that may counteract it. We present an in-silico framework classifying sphingolipids and designed derivatives as candidate membrane-disruptive or candidate protective species, scored against real biological referents using externally published tools rather than a bespoke composite. Its central finding concerns a single, chemically defined difference in lipid state. In coarse-grained (MARTINI 3) molecular d
papers.summary: This paper presents an in-silico framework for classifying sphingolipids and designed derivatives as either membrane-disruptive or membrane-protective, using published tools rather than a custom composite score. Its central claim is that enzymatic N-deacylation acts as a predicted membrane-disruption switch for sphingomyelin, framed as a falsifiable hypothesis relevant to sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, this study identifies a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state marked by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. The authors show this niche can be targeted pharmacologically with ipragliflozin, suggesting a potentially druggable axis linking vascular aging to age-related disease.

papers.title: Lightweight 2D-Convolutional Neural Network for Drug-Kinase Binding Affinity Prediction with Minimal Encoded Representations.
papers.abstract: Drug-kinase binding affinity (DKBA) prediction plays a crucial role in prioritizing compounds and reducing the time and financial resources required for drug discovery. However, many existing deep learning models rely on complex molecular representations, such as molecular graphs or pretrained embeddings, which may increase computational complexity and limit scalability.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
papers.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight 2D-convolutional neural network for predicting drug-kinase binding affinity using minimal encoded molecular representations, avoiding complex graph-based or pretrained embedding approaches. The goal is to reduce computational complexity and improve scalability while maintaining predictive performance for compound prioritization in drug discovery.

papers.title: Advances in deep learning for antimicrobial research.
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance and the lag in the development of new antimicrobial drugs have become major challenges for global public health. Conventional methods for discovering antimicrobial drugs are characterized by long development cycles and high costs, which are further exacerbated by the rapid evolution of bacterial resistance. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop efficient computational methods to accelerate the identification of drug resistance mechanisms and the research and development process of new antimicrobial drugs. In recent years, the new generation
papers.summary: This review discusses how deep learning methods are being applied to antimicrobial research, particularly to accelerate the discovery of new antimicrobial drugs and the identification of drug resistance mechanisms. It highlights the need for efficient computational approaches given the long, costly traditional drug development pipelines and the rapid evolution of bacterial resistance.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be combined with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It outlines a workflow from mining biomedical data resources through AI-driven prediction to experimental validation of plant-derived compounds. The paper argues that AI can help overcome the chemical complexity and mechanistic gaps that have limited translation of botanical drugs into modern cardiovascular therapeutics.

papers.title: A survey on ethical digital twins in healthcare.
papers.abstract: Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), defined as dynamic, data-driven, in silico representations of individuals, organs, medical devices, clinical workflows, or healthcare systems, are emerging as a promising paradigm for transforming healthcare. DT4H systems have the potential to advance personalized medicine, treatment optimization, disease prediction, drug discovery, clinical trials, and health system planning. However, their real-world development and deployment also raise important ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI). Because DT4H systems rely on sensitive longitudinal health data a
papers.summary: This survey examines the ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) of Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), which are dynamic, data-driven virtual representations of individuals, organs, or healthcare systems. It highlights how these systems could advance personalized medicine, drug discovery, and health planning while raising concerns around sensitive longitudinal health data. The paper maps the ethical landscape and likely proposes governance or design principles for responsible DT4H development.

papers.title: Analysis of novel umami peptides in Dengchuan beef and their taste mechanism: Integrated peptidomics, machine learning and molecular simulation studies.
papers.abstract: This study revealed the umami peptides in Dengchuan beef (DB) and its umami mechanism through peptidomics combined with molecular simulation technology. A total of 4220 peptides were identified by LC-MS/MS, among which five novel umami peptides (ER-10, GK-10, DR-11, EA-11, and HY-12) were screened via virtual screening. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue analysis confirmed the umami properties of these peptides, with ER-10 and DR-11 exhibiting significant umami-enhancing effects. Molecular simulations revealed that Lys155, Gln52, Ser109, Ser216, Arg255, Ser217 and Met151 were identified
papers.summary: This study identified 4220 peptides in Dengchuan beef using LC-MS/MS peptidomics and screened five novel umami peptides (ER-10, GK-10, DR-11, EA-11, HY-12) via virtual screening. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue analysis confirmed their umami taste, with ER-10 and DR-11 showing strong umami-enhancing effects. Molecular simulations revealed key binding residues (Lys155, Gln52, Ser109, Ser216, Arg255, Ser217, Met151) underlying the taste mechanism.

papers.title: Cutting-edge developments in computer-aided anti-HIV drug design.
papers.abstract: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), remains a major global public health issue. Current antiretroviral therapy (ART) does not fully eradicate HIV infection, and the virus can establish latent reservoirs in the body that are challenging to eliminate. Consequently, the development of new anti-HIV medications remains a critical necessity. Traditional drug development methods are time-consuming, financially demanding, and carry a high risk of failure. In contrast, computer-aided drug design (CADD) offers a promising alternative by leveraging
papers.summary: This review surveys recent advances in computer-aided drug design (CADD) approaches for developing new anti-HIV therapies, motivated by the fact that current antiretroviral treatment cannot fully eradicate the virus due to latent reservoirs. It highlights how computational methods can accelerate and reduce the cost of identifying new drug candidates compared to traditional development pipelines.

papers.title: Extra-nasal odorant receptors: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Since the first demonstration of extra-nasal odorant receptor (OR) function of OR1D2 (hOR17-4) in human sperm, ORs have emerged as a widely distributed receptor family. ORs are now known to be belonged to a family of seven transmembrane domain G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) expressed across diverse extra-nasal tissues, including skin, gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune cells, and tumors. In these tissues, ORs act as metabolite- and environment-sensitive sensors that translate chemical cues into tissue-specific signaling pathways that regulate proliferati
papers.summary: This review consolidates evidence that odorant receptors (ORs), a large family of GPCRs, are expressed well beyond the nose—in skin, gut, kidney, cardiovascular tissue, liver, immune cells, and tumors—where they sense metabolites and environmental chemicals to regulate processes like proliferation. It discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying these extra-nasal functions and their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: An interpretable consensus pipeline for candidate dopamine D2 receptor ligands.
papers.abstract: Machine learning accelerates GPCR ligand discovery but often lacks interpretability and struggles to generalise to structurally novel chemical space. We present an integrated framework combining ensemble learning, SHAP interpretability, and complementary structure-based analyses to prioritise putative candidates for the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2). Models were trained on 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds using Bemis-Murcko scaffold-split validation. Feature ablation showed that Morgan fingerprints alone were sufficient for classification (AUC = 0.910), whereas combined physicochemical descriptors
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning pipeline for identifying candidate dopamine D2 receptor ligands, combining ensemble learning, SHAP interpretability, and structure-based analyses. Using 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds with scaffold-split validation, the authors found that Morgan fingerprints alone achieved strong classification performance (AUC = 0.910). The framework aims to improve generalizability and interpretability in GPCR ligand discovery.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study used a 3D CNN-CVAE combined with LSTM-based molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived compounds targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened via pocket prediction, docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates an AI-driven de novo design pipeline for dopaminergic drug candidates.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 29 flavonoids and one FDA-approved drug for their ability to inhibit PCSK9, a key target for lowering cholesterol. Using drug-likeness filters, ADMET predictions, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors identified promising flavonoid candidates that bind PCSK9 strongly. The work suggests natural flavonoids could be further explored as lipid-lowering agents, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation methods to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins linked to non-small cell lung cancer. The authors identify candidate compounds that may bind key oncogenic targets, suggesting these natural products warrant further experimental testing as low-toxicity anticancer agents.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This preclinical study identifies a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a lead candidate for prostate cancer treatment, developed through molecular hybridization of pharmacologically active heterocycles. The compound was evaluated using integrated mechanistic approaches to assess its anticancer activity, addressing the need for new therapies in androgen deprivation therapy-resistant disease.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that AI-driven drug repurposing has been overly focused on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism validation, safety assessment, and translational testing. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism awareness and safety validation into AI repurposing pipelines.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study used network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, then virtually screened 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Three top candidate compounds (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) were identified with favorable docking scores, suggesting potential natural modulators of TLR4-driven hyperinflammation.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of FDA-approved compounds against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme for viral DNA replication. The authors identify candidate compounds that could be repurposed as antiviral therapies for mpox, addressing the current lack of targeted treatments.

papers.title: Large-scale virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals identifies multiple CDR1 binders and reveals Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a putative CDR1-GSC1 dual-target lead against Candida albicans with initial in-vitro evidence.
papers.abstract: The increasing incidence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans, mainly mediated by multidrug efflux transporters and alterations of cell-wall biosynthesis, requires the discovery of new antifungal compounds targeting multiple pathways involved in resistance. In the present study, we employed an integrated computational-experimental workflow to identify potential antifungal phytochemicals from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) database. In the virtual screening, a total of 17,967 phytochemicals were screened against the ATP-binding cassette efflux tran
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 17,967 phytochemicals from the IMPPAT database against the Candida albicans efflux pump CDR1, identifying several binders and highlighting Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a dual-target lead that also binds GSC1, a cell-wall synthesis enzyme. Initial in-vitro experiments support its antifungal potential, suggesting a promising scaffold for overcoming antifungal resistance.

papers.title: Therapeutic Antitoxoplasmosis Potential of Garcinia cambogia: Evidence From In Silico and In Vivo Studies.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii, an opportunistic protozoan, is widely prevalent and poses potential health risks. Its treatment remains challenging with several side effects, urging the exploration of new, safe, and efficient drugs. We aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) against both acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. Sixty Swiss albino mice were allocated into five groups: I (healthy), II (model), III (spiramycin [SPM] treated, IV (GC treated), and V (SPM + GC treated). Each group is further divided into two subgroups receiving treatment at 4 and 42 days p
papers.summary: This study evaluated Garcinia cambogia extract as a treatment for Toxoplasma gondii infection using both computational (in silico) predictions and mouse experiments. Mice treated with the plant extract, alone or combined with the standard drug spiramycin, showed therapeutic effects against acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. The findings suggest G. cambogia may offer a safer alternative or adjunct to current treatments, though the abstract is truncated and full efficacy data are not fully detailed.
